Ring introduces Drone Cam and Rover Cam for mobile security

AI Pilot supports mapping and patrols; U.S. Rover shipments are planned for December, while Drone Cam targets January and awaits FCC authorization.

About Amazon ↗10 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Flying and wheeled security cameras

Ring announced its Ring Robotics category on November 10, comprising the indoor 2K Drone Cam and the business-focused Rover Cam, which streams up to 4K. Both integrate with Ring’s app and devices to inspect places outside fixed cameras’ views.

Mapping and patrols

AI Pilot combines cameras, sensors, vision models and cloud processing to map spaces, suggest patrol points and route around obstacles. Rover has a rising camera mast, lights and a siren. Features including scheduled patrols and reviewing recordings require a compatible Ring Protect plan.

Availability and conditions

Ring lists Rover Cam at $999.99, with U.S. shipments planned from December 16, 2026. Drone Cam is $249.99 and targets January 27, 2027, but remains without FCC authorization according to the announcement. Its camera turns off when docked; Rover’s Sleep Mode retracts the mast and disables the microphone. These are announced capabilities, not independent test results.
